::: {.fi-standfirst}
**FRESH** starts where most health tools stop: what to do when credible sources
disagree. It re-checks what published studies actually show, reconciles expert
rating systems that contradict each other, and estimates risk for particular people
and places instead of a national average. A number without its uncertainty is not
an answer, so the doubt stays on the face of every result. What people believe is
data too, measured against the expert record, which turns the gap between them into
an education agenda rather than a scolding.

Food comes first because that is where expert systems clash most openly, and the
same methods reach the rest of a life, from sleep and movement to social connection,
biological age, and the place you live. Health effort goes to widening access, to
definition fights over what counts as ultraprocessed, to policies that work as
bandages, to pointing at personal behavior, while the information itself gets
treated as solved. It is not. Better information cures nothing on its own, but it is
the cheapest lever almost nobody is pulling. The tools and essays here are open to
anyone who wants to see for themselves, and the longer version of the argument is on
[what we're doing](about.qmd).
:::
